column4: Intranet — an illustrative example inside "including on an intranet or in paper form" promoted to a standalone class, rather than treated as one possible value/instance of Media.
Paper — same issue as above; "in paper form" is an example within a list, not a named domain concept requiring its own class.
Media ◁— Intranet (generalization/inheritance edge) — asserts a formal subtype relationship the prompt never states; the prompt only gives an example, not a taxonomy.
Media ◁— Paper (generalization/inheritance edge) — same issue; inheritance structure invented from an example clause.

Attribute data types invented throughout (e.g., description : String, percentComplete : int, startDate/endDate : Date, name : String on ProjectManager/Platform) — the prompt never specifies any data type.

The reasoning models composition between Scene and Setup, although the prompt only states that a setup is related to a single scene. The ownership/lifecycle semantics implied by composition are not supported by the prompt.

The reasoning models composition between Setup and Take, although the prompt only states that a take is associated with a single setup. Composition introduces unsupported ownership/lifecycle semantics.

The reasoning introduces additional modelling details not explicitly supported by the prompt (e.g., exact multiplicities, data types, abstract classes, visibility, enumeration choice, and other implementation-specific decisions).
The reasoning introduces WordProcessor as a controller/application class. The prompt describes the word processor as the system being modelled, rather than as a separate domain entity.

The reasoning introduces the helper abstraction HeaderFooterItem and the classes TextItem, DateItem, TimeItem, and PageNumberItem. The prompt only states that date, time, and page number may appear in a header or footer; it does not identify them as independent entities. TextItem is not stated at all.
The reasoning introduces the technical interfaces IBodyContent and ICellContent. These are implementation-oriented abstractions not identified in the problem description.
The reasoning introduces the technical interfaces IBodyContent and ICellContent. These are implementation-oriented abstractions not identified in the problem description.

The reasoning introduces SentencePart as an abstract entity grouping words and punctuation. The prompt specifies that sentences contain words and punctuation characters but does not identify a separate sentence-part entity.
The inheritance hierarchy from HeaderFooterItem to TextItem, DateItem, TimeItem, and PageNumberItem is invented. The prompt does not define these concepts as specialisations of a common entity.
The realization relationships connecting Sentence, Picture, and Table to IBodyContent, and TextContent and Picture to ICellContent, introduce an unsupported interface structure.

The inheritance relationships from SentencePart to Word and Punctuation are not specified by the prompt. The containment of words and punctuation within sentences is supported, but the invented generalization is not.

The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, visibilities, data types, method signatures, attributes such as file paths and image dimensions, ordering constraints, and other details not required by the prompt.
The reasoning omits Column from the final model, despite the explicit requirement that tables are made up of both rows and columns.

The reasoning introduces an abstract Staff class. Receptionists, nurses, and doctors are explicitly mentioned, but the prompt does not define a common staff entity or require them to be represented through a shared superclass.
The reasoning introduces inheritance from Staff to Receptionist, Nurse, and Doctor. Their shared generalisation is a modelling assumption not stated or clearly required by the prompt.

The reasoning adds unsupported attributes, operation signatures, exact multiplicities, data types, identifiers, status fields, dosage details, and assumptions such as each appointment being assigned to exactly one doctor and one receptionist.
The reasoning introduces Supplier as a domain entity. The prompt only states that unavailable movies are ordered; it does not mention suppliers or supplier management.
The reasoning introduces RestockOrder as a separate entity. The prompt indicates that unavailable movies are ordered, but does not define a distinct restocking/order entity.
The reasoning introduces Catalogue as an explicit class. The prompt mentions browsing the catalogue, but does not identify the catalogue itself as a domain entity.

The reasoning introduces an inheritance hierarchy between Order, PurchaseOrder, and RentalOrder. The prompt distinguishes buying and hiring operations but does not specify an order generalization hierarchy.

The reasoning introduces a composition relationship between Subscriber and Card. The prompt states that subscribers rent movies with their own rechargeable card, but it does not specify ownership or lifecycle semantics implied by composition.

The reasoning introduces aggregation between Catalogue and Movie. While movies can be browsed through a catalogue, the prompt does not define a structural whole-part relationship between these concepts.
The reasoning introduces structural associations between RestockOrder and both Supplier and Movie. These relationships rely on invented entities and are not supported by the prompt.

The reasoning adds unsupported implementation details such as exact multiplicities, attributes, operation signatures, pricing fields, available copy counts, search operations, identifiers, and other implementation-specific assumptions.

The reasoning introduces CrewRequirement as a separate domain entity with attributes such as minimumCount and requiredMinimumLevel. The prompt describes crew requirements for an aircraft type but does not explicitly define a distinct crew-requirement entity.

The reasoning models composition between AircraftType and CrewRequirement. The prompt supports associating crew-role requirements with an aircraft type, but it does not specify the ownership and lifecycle semantics implied by composition.
The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, enumerations, attribute names, a required-level field, and other modelling decisions not explicitly specified in the prompt.

The reasoning does not structurally connect the pilots assigned to a flight with the role and crew-count requirements of the aircraft type. It models only fixed captain and copilot associations, so it cannot represent additional required roles such as navigator or more than one pilot in a particular role.

The reasoning models composition between Bank and Customer. The prompt supports the bank system storing customer data, but it does not establish the ownership and lifecycle dependency implied by composition.
The reasoning models composition between Customer and Account. The phrase “their accounts” supports an association, but it does not imply that accounts are lifecycle-dependent parts of customers.

The reasoning models composition between InvestmentAccount and StockOrder. The prompt supports stock orders being associated with investment accounts, but it does not specify the strong ownership semantics of composition.
The reasoning adds exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, and modelling assumptions such as zero-or-more accounts and orders.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, identifiers (e.g., serviceId, partId, modelId), data types, public/private visibility, and other implementation-specific modelling decisions not explicitly required by the prompt.
Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, an unsupported mealId, and implementation-level constraints such as {id} and {unique}.
Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, an Urgency enumeration, and the assumption that the package’s drop-off centre may initially be optional.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, and assumptions such as every furniture piece belonging to exactly one furniture line and every order containing at least one order line.

The reasoning introduces Material as a separate entity. The prompt only states that products of the same type use the same material and does not explicitly require materials to be stored as independent entities.

The reasoning introduces a structural association between Product and the invented Material entity. The prompt supports storing the material of a product type, but not necessarily as a separate relationship.
The reasoning introduces a many-to-many association between Worker and the invented Skill entity. The prompt only requires storing each worker’s skills.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, optionality notation, generated identifiers, and additional attributes such as Product.name that are not explicitly specified.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, visibility, a generated rental identifier, an enumeration implementation for bicycle type, and assumptions about which fields are optional.
The reasoning introduces ParkingSystem (or CarParkController) as a controller entity. The prompt describes the system behaviour but does not identify the controller itself as a domain entity.
The reasoning introduces ExitSensor as a separate entity. The prompt only states that the exit barrier is automatically raised; it does not mention a sensor.

The reasoning introduces aggregation/composition between ParkingSystem and Card (maintaining a collection of known cards). The prompt states that card numbers are verified but does not specify this structural ownership relationship.

The reasoning introduces structural associations between ParkingSystem and Barrier, CardReader, Sign, and CarPark. These controller relationships are implementation decisions rather than relationships stated or reasonably implied by the domain description.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, controller methods, internal collections (e.g., knownCards), visibility, implementation-oriented operations, and additional attributes such as isReturned and occupiedSpaces.
The reasoning introduces Bank (OOBank) as an explicit domain entity. The prompt describes OOBank as the organization being modelled, but does not require a separate Bank class.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, visibility, data types, identifiers, enumerations for privileges, parent–child hierarchy implementation, and other implementation-specific modelling decisions.

Exist. The reasoning adds implementation details such as visibility modifiers, constructor signatures, class and field names, delegation structure, and the aggregation notation between ContractDecorator and Contract.
The reasoning introduces a Library–User relationship labelled registers. The prompt identifies library users but does not state that the library registers or structurally contains them.
Exist. The reasoning adds exact multiplicities, data types, an unsupported Library.name attribute, and the additional constraint that a book can have at most one active borrowing at a time.

Exist. The reasoning introduces exact multiplicities, data types, identifiers, visibility, method signatures, and unsupported attributes such as hospital name, office location, doctor specialty, and patient insurance number.
